🇮🇳 India is preparing to put corporate bonds onchain

India plans to launch its first tokenised corporate bond issuance in September, according to Reuters.

The pilot will involve state-owned power financier REC and bonds worth less than 5 billion rupees, approximately $57 million.

Blockchain will be used to record:

• issuance
• ownership
• trading
• settlement

Investors will purchase the bonds using India’s wholesale central bank digital currency. They will need both a CBDC wallet and a new digital securities wallet called DEMAT 2.0.

The pilot will initially be available only to selected investors. A secondary market is expected to follow in December.

The important point is that these bonds are not being turned into speculative crypto assets.

They remain regulated debt instruments. Blockchain changes the infrastructure behind them by allowing ownership and settlement to be recorded on the same digital system.

This is where tokenisation becomes practical.

The asset remains familiar.

The process behind it becomes faster and more programmable.

🔗 Source: Reuters⁠

THEY TOOK THE “POWER UNITS” FROM HER LEG—AND INJECTED THEM INTO HER BLIND EYES.

What happened next has opened a completely new door in medicine.

A 26-year-old woman had suffered a devastating brain hemorrhage. The damage reached her optic nerves and retina, leaving her almost completely blind.

For 71 days before the procedure, doctors performed 45 automated tests.

Not one showed a normal pupil response to light.

Then the medical team tried something never previously reported in a human eye.

They removed a small piece of muscle from her leg.

From that tissue, they isolated fresh mitochondria—the microscopic structures that produce energy inside our cells.

The mitochondria were then injected directly into both eyes, 24 hours apart.

Within days, her pupils began responding to light again.

After treatment, 13 of 52 measurements reached the normal-response threshold. She was also reported to perceive shapes and shadows through her left eye.

But here is the part that matters:

The effect faded after approximately four weeks, and the procedure did not restore measurable vision.

This was one patient. The report has not yet completed peer review. It is not proof of a cure.

Yet the experiment crossed a boundary that would have sounded impossible not long ago:

Instead of replacing an entire damaged cell, scientists attempted to rescue it by transferring new biological “power units” into the tissue.

The question is no longer whether living mitochondria can be placed inside the human eye.

They already have been.

The real question is whether the effect can one day be made strong enough—and last long enough—to save vision.

🚨 AIR FORCE MAJOR CRIMINALLY CHARGED UNDER THE UCMJ AFTER PUBLICLY ATTACKING TRUMP

Active-duty Air Force Maj. Jason Watson has been formally charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) after publicly criticizing President Trump and calling for his impeachment — including while wearing his uniform during a protest at the U.S. Capitol. (cbsnews.com)

Watson faces 10 alleged violations across three UCMJ articles:

• 3 counts — Article 88: Contemptuous words against the President or other specified officials.
• 5 counts — Article 92: Failure to obey lawful orders or regulations.
• 2 counts — Article 133: Conduct unbecoming an officer. (ktvz.com)

⚖️ Article 88 is particularly significant. It specifically restricts commissioned officers from using contemptuous words against the President, Vice President, Congress and certain other officials. According to Watson’s attorneys, he is believed to be among the first officers of his rank in U.S. military history charged under Article 88. (cbsnews.com)

Watson was initially detained July 1 after appearing in uniform on the Capitol steps carrying a sign calling to “Impeach. Convict. Remove” President Trump. He was detained again following another public interview criticizing Trump. (cbsnews.com)

The Air Force says Watson will remain in pretrial confinement while the military justice process proceeds. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty under the UCMJ. (cbsnews.com)
